channel_b.verbatim: Lord Clement-Jones (LD), House of Lords, 16 June 2026: "My Lords, the Minister has mentioned the AI Security Institute. It identified ways to circumvent the safety guardrails of Fable 5 and Mythos before their public launch, including vulnerabilities that could allow the extraction of instructions for producing dangerous substances, yet the model was released by Anthropic regardless. Will the Minister now accept that voluntary co-operation with safety institutes is wholly insufficient at this level of capability and bring forward legislation giving the AI Security Institute the statutory power, where necessary, to delay or prevent the launch of dangerous frontier AI models in the UK?" — Ministerial reply, Baroness Lloyd of Effra (Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State, DBT/DSIT): "The AI Security Institute did test Mythos and Fable before they were launched. In light of the risks that they potentially posed—Mythos in particular—we also gave advice to our companies. We worked carefully with the National Cyber Security Centre to provide advice to companies and regulators on what needed to be done…"
channel_b.policy_response: UK Parliament (Lords) engaged directly with UK AISI's pre-launch red-teaming result on Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 — that AISI found ways to circumvent the models' safety guardrails before public launch and that Anthropic released anyway — and used it as the basis for a demand that AISI be given statutory power to delay or prevent frontier-model launches. The responding DSIT/DBT minister confirmed on the record that AISI tested both models pre-launch and that, in light of the risks, the Government issued advice to companies and regulators jointly with the NCSC. This is official parliamentary and ministerial engagement with the finding; it created no enforceable obligation (the Government declined to legislate and restated reliance on sector regulators), so it is non-binding.
channel_b.reasoning: Upgrade from 'No policy uptake identified'. The previous pass recorded a clean UK negative; that is wrong. The 16 June 2026 Lords PNQ contains a member explicitly stating the substance of AISI's safeguard-circumvention result on the two named systems ('identified ways to circumvent the safety guardrails of Fable 5 and Mythos before their public launch'), which is precisely this finding's subject matter — AISI red-teamers breaking Fable 5's safeguards within hours of access. It clears the strict admissibility bar because it references the evaluator's specific result on the named system, not AI risk in general or AISI as an organisation. The domain Lord Clement-Jones highlights (dangerous-substance instructions) is a sibling result in the same AISI safeguards section of the system card as the cyberoffensive jailbreak, which is why I record this as medium rather than high confidence. No binding instrument followed: the Minister declined the legislative ask.
